note: Generic OBD-II fault codes (SAE J2012 numbering) with plain-language explanations written for this app. drive: yes = safe to drive, get it checked when convenient; carefully = drive gently and get it checked soon; no = don't drive, get help. Codes not listed are explained by their family; manufacturer-specific codes need the service centre's tool.

P0011.title: Intake camshaft timing over-advanced (bank 1)
P0011.plain: The engine computer sees the intake camshaft timing ahead of where it should be.

P0016.title: Crankshaft and camshaft position don't match (bank 1)
P0016.plain: The engine's two position sensors disagree, so the timing may be off.

P0087.title: Fuel rail pressure too low
P0087.plain: The fuel system can't build enough pressure; the engine may lose power or stall.

P0088.title: Fuel rail pressure too high
P0088.plain: Fuel pressure is above the limit.

P0093.title: Fuel system large leak detected
P0093.plain: The engine computer suspects a big fuel leak.

P0101.title: Air flow sensor (MAF) reading out of range
P0101.plain: The sensor that measures air going into the engine reads values that don't make sense.
causes: Air leak after the air filter

P0102.title: Air flow sensor (MAF) signal low
P0102.plain: The air flow sensor's signal is too low.

P0106.title: Manifold pressure sensor (MAP) reading out of range
P0106.plain: The sensor that measures pressure in the intake reads values that don't make sense.

P0108.title: Manifold pressure sensor (MAP) signal high
P0108.plain: The intake pressure sensor's signal is too high.

P0113.title: Intake air temperature sensor signal high
P0113.plain: The intake air temperature sensor reads as if disconnected.

P0117.title: Coolant temperature sensor signal low
P0117.plain: The engine temperature sensor reads impossibly hot; the fan may run all the time.

P0118.title: Coolant temperature sensor signal high
P0118.plain: The engine temperature sensor reads as if disconnected; the temperature gauge may be wrong.

P0121.title: Throttle position sensor reading out of range
P0121.plain: The throttle position sensor gives readings that don't match the engine.

P0122.title: Throttle position sensor signal low
P0122.plain: The throttle position signal is too low; the engine may go into a limited-power mode.

P0123.title: Throttle position sensor signal high
P0123.plain: The throttle position signal is too high; the engine may go into a limited-power mode.

P0128.title: Engine doesn't reach its working temperature
P0128.plain: The engine takes too long to warm up, usually because the thermostat stays open.

P0130.title: Oxygen sensor circuit (bank 1, sensor 1)
P0130.plain: The oxygen sensor before the catalytic converter isn't working right.

P0131.title: Oxygen sensor voltage low (bank 1, sensor 1)
P0131.plain: The front oxygen sensor's signal stays too low.

P0133.title: Oxygen sensor slow response (bank 1, sensor 1)
P0133.plain: The front oxygen sensor reacts slowly; fuel economy can suffer.

P0135.title: Oxygen sensor heater (bank 1, sensor 1)
P0135.plain: The heater inside the front oxygen sensor isn't working.

P0141.title: Oxygen sensor heater (bank 1, sensor 2)
P0141.plain: The heater inside the rear oxygen sensor isn't working.

P0171.title: Engine running too lean (bank 1)
P0171.plain: The engine is getting too much air or too little fuel. Mileage and smoothness can suffer.
causes: Weak fuel pump or clogged fuel filter

P0172.title: Engine running too rich (bank 1)
P0172.plain: The engine is getting too much fuel. Mileage drops and the exhaust may smell of fuel.
causes: Dirty air filter or air flow sensor

P0174.title: Engine running too lean (bank 2)
P0174.plain: The second cylinder bank gets too much air or too little fuel.

P0175.title: Engine running too rich (bank 2)
P0175.plain: The second cylinder bank gets too much fuel.

P0190.title: Fuel rail pressure sensor circuit
P0190.plain: The fuel pressure sensor's signal is faulty.

P0200.title: Injector circuit
P0200.plain: One of the fuel injector circuits has a fault.

P0201.title: Injector circuit, cylinder 1
P0201.plain: The fuel injector for cylinder 1 has an electrical fault; that cylinder may not work.

P0217.title: Engine overheating
P0217.plain: The engine temperature went above its safe limit.

P0219.title: Engine over-revved
P0219.plain: The engine went faster than its safe limit, for example after a missed gear.

P0230.title: Fuel pump circuit
P0230.plain: The fuel pump's electrical circuit has a fault; the car may not start or may stall.

P0234.title: Turbo over-boost
P0234.plain: The turbocharger is producing more boost than allowed; the engine may limit power.
causes: Sticking wastegate or boost control valve

P0299.title: Turbo under-boost
P0299.plain: The turbocharger isn't producing enough boost; the car feels slow.
causes: Boost leak in a hose or intercooler

P0300.title: Random misfires
P0300.plain: Several cylinders are misfiring. If the engine light is flashing, slow down and get it checked now: misfires can damage the catalytic converter.
causes: Worn spark plugs or ignition coils

P0301.title: Misfire in cylinder 1
causes: Spark plug or ignition coil for cylinder 1

P0302.title: Misfire in cylinder 2
causes: Spark plug or ignition coil for cylinder 2

P0303.title: Misfire in cylinder 3
causes: Spark plug or ignition coil for cylinder 3

P0304.title: Misfire in cylinder 4
causes: Spark plug or ignition coil for cylinder 4

P0305.title: Misfire in cylinder 5
causes: Spark plug or ignition coil for cylinder 5

P0306.title: Misfire in cylinder 6
causes: Spark plug or ignition coil for cylinder 6

P0325.title: Knock sensor circuit (bank 1)
P0325.plain: The sensor that listens for engine knock has a fault; the engine may run with less power to be safe.

P0335.title: Crankshaft position sensor circuit
P0335.plain: The engine can't read the crankshaft position; it may stall or not start.

P0340.title: Camshaft position sensor circuit (bank 1)
P0340.plain: The engine can't read the camshaft position; it may start slowly or run roughly.

P0351.title: Ignition coil A circuit
P0351.plain: The ignition coil for one cylinder has an electrical fault.

P0352.title: Ignition coil B circuit
P0352.plain: The ignition coil for one cylinder has an electrical fault.

P0380.title: Glow plug circuit
P0380.plain: The diesel engine's glow plug heating has a fault; cold starts may be hard.

P0400.title: Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) flow
P0400.plain: The EGR system, which feeds some exhaust back to reduce emissions, isn't flowing as expected.

P0401.title: EGR flow too low
P0401.plain: Too little exhaust is going back through the EGR system, often because of carbon build-up.

P0402.title: EGR flow too high
P0402.plain: Too much exhaust is going back through the EGR system; the engine may idle roughly.

P0403.title: EGR control circuit
P0403.plain: The EGR valve's electrical circuit has a fault.

P0420.title: Catalytic converter efficiency low (bank 1)
P0420.plain: The catalytic converter isn't cleaning the exhaust as well as it should. Not urgent, but the car may fail its PUC test.
causes: An engine fault (misfire) damaged the converter

P0430.title: Catalytic converter efficiency low (bank 2)
P0430.plain: The second catalytic converter isn't cleaning the exhaust well.

P0440.title: Fuel vapour system (EVAP) fault
P0440.plain: The system that traps petrol vapour from the tank has a fault. Harmless to drive, but it adds emissions.

P0442.title: Small leak in the fuel vapour system
P0442.plain: A small leak lets petrol vapour escape.
causes: Fuel cap not closed or worn seal

P0443.title: Fuel vapour purge valve circuit
P0443.plain: The valve that sends petrol vapour to the engine has an electrical fault.

P0446.title: Fuel vapour vent control circuit
P0446.plain: The fuel vapour vent valve isn't working.

P0455.title: Large leak in the fuel vapour system
P0455.plain: Petrol vapour is escaping, often simply because the fuel cap is open or loose.

P0456.title: Very small leak in the fuel vapour system
P0456.plain: A tiny vapour leak, often from the fuel cap seal.
causes: Small crack in a vapour hose

P0457.title: Fuel cap loose or off
P0457.plain: The fuel cap isn't closed properly. Tighten it until it clicks; the light goes off after some driving.
causes: Fuel cap loose, missing or worn

P0480.title: Radiator fan control circuit
P0480.plain: The radiator fan's control circuit has a fault; the engine may overheat in traffic.

P0500.title: Vehicle speed sensor
P0500.plain: The car can't read its speed properly; the speedometer, cruise control or ABS may be affected.

P0505.title: Idle control system
P0505.plain: The engine can't hold a steady idle.
causes: Dirty throttle body or idle valve

P0506.title: Idle speed lower than expected
P0506.plain: The engine idles too slowly and may stall.

P0520.title: Oil pressure sensor circuit
P0520.plain: The oil pressure sensor or its wiring has a fault. Check the oil level; if the oil light comes on, stop the engine.

P0524.title: Engine oil pressure too low
P0524.plain: The engine isn't getting enough oil pressure. Running it like this can destroy it.

P0562.title: System voltage low
P0562.plain: The car's electrical voltage is too low; the battery isn't being charged properly.

P0563.title: System voltage high
P0563.plain: The car's electrical voltage is too high, which can damage electronics and the battery.

P0600.title: Control module communication fault
P0600.plain: The engine computer has trouble talking to another control unit.

P0601.title: Engine computer memory error
P0601.plain: The engine computer found an error in its own memory.
causes: Engine computer needs reprogramming or replacement

P0606.title: Engine computer processor fault
P0606.plain: The engine computer found a fault in itself.

P0627.title: Fuel pump control circuit
P0627.plain: The fuel pump's control circuit has a fault; the engine may stall.

P0700.title: Gearbox fault (ask the gearbox computer)
P0700.plain: The gearbox computer has stored its own fault code; the gearbox may be in a limp mode.
causes: Any gearbox fault: the service centre reads the gearbox computer

P0715.title: Gearbox input speed sensor
P0715.plain: The automatic gearbox can't read its input speed; shifts may be harsh.

P0730.title: Wrong gear ratio
P0730.plain: The automatic gearbox isn't in the gear it should be, or is slipping.

P0741.title: Torque converter clutch stuck off
P0741.plain: The automatic gearbox's lock-up clutch doesn't engage; mileage on highways drops.

P2002.title: Diesel particulate filter efficiency low
P2002.plain: The diesel particulate filter isn't trapping soot as it should.

P2096.title: Fuel trim after the catalytic converter too lean (bank 1)
P2096.plain: The rear oxygen sensor sees too much oxygen after the catalytic converter.

P2135.title: Throttle position sensors disagree
P2135.plain: The two throttle position sensors give different readings; the engine may limit power to be safe.

P2138.title: Accelerator pedal sensors disagree
P2138.plain: The two accelerator pedal sensors give different readings; the engine may limit power to be safe.

P2187.title: Engine too lean at idle (bank 1)
P2187.plain: At idle the engine gets too much air, usually from a vacuum leak.

P2188.title: Engine too rich at idle (bank 1)
P2188.plain: At idle the engine gets too much fuel.

P2195.title: Oxygen sensor stuck lean (bank 1, sensor 1)
P2195.plain: The front oxygen sensor keeps reading lean.

P242F.title: Diesel particulate filter: ash build-up
P242F.plain: The diesel particulate filter is clogged with ash that driving can't burn off.
causes: Filter at the end of its life

P2463.title: Diesel particulate filter: soot build-up
P2463.plain: The diesel particulate filter is full of soot. A steady 20-minute highway drive often clears it; if not, get it cleaned.

U0001.title: High-speed CAN network fault
U0001.plain: The car's main data network has a fault; several systems may show warnings.
causes: Wiring or connector on the network

U0073.title: Control module network off
U0073.plain: A control unit stopped talking on the car's network.

U0100.title: Lost communication with the engine computer
U0100.plain: Other units can't hear the engine computer. Often caused by a weak battery or a loose connector.

U0121.title: Lost communication with the ABS unit
U0121.plain: Other units can't hear the ABS unit; ABS and stability control may be off. Normal braking still works.

U0140.title: Lost communication with the body control unit
U0140.plain: Other units can't hear the body control unit (lights, locks, wipers).
causes: Body control unit power or connector

U0155.title: Lost communication with the instrument cluster
U0155.plain: Other units can't hear the instrument cluster; warning lights may not show.

C0035.title: Front left wheel speed sensor
C0035.plain: ABS can't read the front left wheel's speed; ABS and stability control may be off.

C0040.title: Front right wheel speed sensor
C0040.plain: ABS can't read the front right wheel's speed; ABS and stability control may be off.

C0045.title: Rear left wheel speed sensor
C0045.plain: ABS can't read the rear left wheel's speed; ABS and stability control may be off.

C0050.title: Rear right wheel speed sensor
C0050.plain: ABS can't read the rear right wheel's speed; ABS and stability control may be off.
